hinweis_de: KI-generierte Pilotbilder, nicht geprüft und nicht in der App. Bildliche Deutung, keine Darstellung historischer Tatsachen.

bilder.prompt: Fine-art oil painting with dramatic chiaroscuro in the tradition of 17th-century Dutch and Italian masters, rich glazes, visible confident brushwork, warm earthy palette with luminous accents, deep shadows, anatomically correct figures, believable perspective and space, museum-quality composition. Night, the courtyard of a modest Galilean house during a wedding feast. In the foreground Mary leans close to Jesus and quietly tells him the wine has run out, her hand resting on his forearm, her face worried. Jesus sits at a low table and turns his face towards her, calm and thoughtful, his expression clearly visible. Beside them an empty clay wine jar lies tipped over next to empty cups. In the softly blurred background, guests are celebrating, dancing and talking under strings of oil lamps. Characters: Mary the mother of Jesus, a woman around fifty, blue veil and blue robe; Jesus, a Galilean man around thirty, dark hair and short beard, white tunic with a deep red mantle, a faint thin golden halo with a subtle cross inside it. Lighting: warm oil-lamp light from the left, cool blue moonlight from the open courtyard on the right. Camera: eye level of a seated person, medium close shot, shallow depth of field. Emotional core: an intimate, urgent whisper amid the noise of the feast. Jesus: his face fully visible and clearly painted like everyone else's, a real human face with warm, expressive eyes and a natural expression fitting the moment. Historically plausible first-century Judea and Galilee: simple woven garments, sandals, stone and clay. Emotional, expressive body language. No text, no letters, no captions, no watermark, no signature, no frame. No modern objects, no text, no extra halos on anyone except Jesus. Avoid: text, letters, watermark, signature, cartoon, anime, childish, cute, plastic 3d render, extra fingers, deformed hands, distorted faces, modern clothing, European medieval armour.
